title: Synthetic traffic replay-driven upgrade harness and reversible patch flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a reusable upgrade harness for Private (VPC) data plane/runtime upgrades that validates changes using synthetic traffic replay, enforces transactional checkpointing for reversible patch flows, and gates terraform/apply with probe-driven health quorum scoring.
background: Customers running Redwood Private must be able to apply runtime patches and version upgrades without application-visible downtime. Existing strategies rely on targeted rollforward/rollback playbooks and health probes, but we lack a standardized harness that (1) replays representative synthetic traffic to validate behavior under realistic load, (2) captures lightweight transactional checkpoints for fast rollback (snapshot of KV/priming state), and (3) integrates with terraform modules to refuse apply unless health quorum and synthetics pass.
goals: Create a harness that can replay tenant-scoped synthetic traffic workloads against a candidate runtime during canary and staged upgrades
Add a transactional checkpoint step (priming snapshot + minimal KV state capture) before any destructive change that allows a fast unwind
Implement a probe quorum evaluator that aggregates synthetic pass/fail, smoke metrics, and live connection liveness to gate terraform apply or automated traffic shift
Expose an operator-friendly CLI and terraform hook that returns non-zero when gating fails
Ship documentation and a runbook for on-call and PMC to execute emergency unwind
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs a configurable synthetic traffic profile (seq length distribution, concurrency mix) against new runtime and reports pass/fail within target window
Checkpoint artifacts (priming snapshot + KV diff) are stored in the customer-managed S3/GCS location and tagged with upgrade ID
Terraform module provides a pre-apply hook that fails if probe quorum isn't met; CI runs the hook in dry-run mode
Automated rollback completes within configured RTO for at least 95% of canary slices in staging tests
Runbook drafted and validated in two staging tenants; post-mortem template included
design_decisions: Use synthetic traffic replay rather than full production mirroring to avoid exposing PII and to keep execution lightweight
Store checkpoints as incremental priming snapshots + KV diffs to minimize snapshot size and speed up restore
Probe quorum will be configurable with weighted signals: synthetic success (50%), latency SLO pass (30%), connection liveness (20%)
Integrate the gating as a terraform external data source that calls the harness CLI; this keeps modules provider-agnostic
Keep default retention for checkpoints to 24 hours but make it configurable per customer
tradeoffs: Synthetic replay covers a representative subset of workloads but may miss rare edge prompts—mitigate with periodic longer replay suites
Checkpointing KV diffs reduces storage but requires careful reconciliation logic on restore; chosen for speed over absolute fidelity
Tighter quorum thresholds reduce risk but increase false positives (blocked upgrades); selected sane defaults with easy overrides
Keeping the hook as an external process avoids deep provider changes but adds an operational dependency to the upgrade pipeline
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): PoC synthetic traffic runner + simple success/failure metrics against canary runtime
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Add checkpoint capture (priming snapshot + KV diff), storage lifecycle, and an unapply script for restore
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Terraform external data source + CLI integration; add probe quorum evaluator and configuration
Phase 4 (2 weeks): Staging validation across two private tenants, runbook iteration, and prepare release notes
Phase 5 (1 week): Security review, customer-facing docs, and on-call drill
risks: Checkpoint restore complexity may cause inconsistency for long-running sessions—mitigation: limit supported session types and document caveats
Synthetic traffic might overload small tenants if not rate-limited—mitigation: tenant-scoped caps and canary window enforcement
Operator error in running the harness could lead to blocked upgrades—mitigation: sane defaults and CI gating
Dependency on customer-managed storage for checkpoints could fail—mitigation: S3/GCS verification step before apply
testing_plan: Unit tests: synthetic runner, checkpoint writer/reader, quorum evaluator
Integration tests: full harness against staging runtime with injected failures (latency spike, KV miss, model load failure)
Chaos tests: network partition between control plane and runtime during upgrade
Load tests: replay scaled traffic equal to 1.2x expected tenant peak to validate safety margins
